notes: The follower slot is one thing shared by three families - the pet cats, the boss pets and the
skilling pets - and until this round the whole lifecycle lived inside the CAT QUEST
(quests/quest_fluffs/scripts/pet.rs2). Every follower in the game went through it with the cat
parts still attached, and two of those parts were not subtle: the login respawn ended with
npc_say("Meeeew!") and settimer(petcat_growth, 150), so a Prince black dragon said "Meow!"
every 90 seconds; and ~follower_death deleted the follower and cleared %follower_obj without
returning the item, so dying with a pet out DESTROYED a 1-in-3,000 drop. It is
npc/scripts/follower.rs2 now, and the cat extras are dispatched POSITIVELY on the item's
category, so a family added later without reading that file gets the plain path.
probita: dying with a pet out still loses it - that is Old School's shape - but lost means it is
waiting at Probita's bureau in East Ardougne, and taking it back costs NOTHING. That is current
Old School too: since September 2025 every pet is insured the moment you get one and reclaims
are free, so there is no insurance step to build and no coin sink to balance.
free is checked as CODE rather than prose - her dialogue says the word "cost" precisely in
order to say there is not one - so the checks are that no currency symbol appears in her script
and that the reclaim handler touches no inv but the store and the pack.
Her art is OSRS npc 5906's own, seven body models and two chatheads on the 377 human
animations - the same pairing the estate agent and the sawmill operator already use - and
model_sha1 pins all nine, because they are a deterministic function of the cache.
She stands in the empty one-room building immediately east of Aemad's Adventuring Supplies,
which is where Old School puts her ("the small building next to Aemad's"). tile is that room's
middle and aemad_tile is the shop's own spawn, both in maps/m40_51.jm2: the check that the two
are within reach of each other is what makes the placement a measurement rather than a memory.
grid: lostpet_store's size and the window's slot count are ONE number. A store slot her window
cannot show is a pet nobody can reclaim, so a 21st pet item has to grow both, and the check
fails until it does.
cat_categories: the three categories the cache's own cat ITEMS carry. ~follower_is_cat names
exactly these, every follower item in all.obj carries one of them, and no pet item carries any -
which is what makes the dispatch safe in both directions.
rings: a pet with more than one look is a RING of npc records joined by param=metamorph_next -
each names the next, the last names the base again. One param covers a pair and a fifteen
alike. Two kinds of ring, and the difference is the design: forms that SHARE ONE ITEM need
%pet_form to remember which one you are on (the item cannot say), and forms that ARE DIFFERENT
ITEMS - TzRek-Jad and JalRek-Jad - need nothing, because the slot's own %follower_obj is the
other item now. bits is the %pet_form range for the first kind and null for the second; the
checks are that each range holds its own ring, that no two overlap, and that ~pet_form_get and
~pet_form_set name the same items in the same order - a get without a set is a form that is
chosen and then forgotten.
The forms themselves are OSRS's own art: 6638 (green, wingless) for the kalphite princess,
6817 the Great blue heron, 6756/6758/6759 the red, black and gold chinchompas, and 7355-7367
plus 8028 for the rift guardian's fourteen recolours. Only the green kalphite princess has
animations of its own (6239/6238); every other form shares its base's pair, which is also what
keeps the client's walk-merge working.
talk: twenty pets, one voice each, three lines each, dispatched on the pet's ITEM so that every
metamorphosis form answers as itself for free. The lines are written for this server rather
than copied out of Old School's transcripts - same shape, our own words. ~chatnpc leaves the
npc on playerfaceclose, so a pet that has spoken would stand there for good: ~follower_refollow
puts it back, and playerfollow is still set in exactly one file.
variants: three pets change their look WITHOUT a right-click, and the cache says so by giving
none of their records a Metamorphosis op. The rock golem takes the colour of an ore you use on
it (a plain rock puts it back, and nothing is consumed); the tangleroot takes a seed and EATS
it; and the rift guardian takes the colour of the altar you were crafting at. They are still
rings, because that is how %pet_form remembers a look through a pick-up and a login, and the
op4 flag on each ring is what says whether anything cycles it.
golem_exact_matches: nine of the eleven ore looks share an EXACT recolour destination with the
ore item's own recolour. Clay and iron are the only tan and dark-brown looks left once those
nine are taken, and the renders agree. Eight of Old School's nineteen ores are not in this
build at all, so neither are their looks.
rift: crafting at an altar unlocks that colour for good (%rift_unlocked, one bit per form
index), the right-click only cycles unlocked colours, and Locking - the cache's own op5 - stops
the altar repainting the pet without stopping the right-click. Eleven altars, eleven colours;
the plain one comes from making a tiara, which rolls the pet with no altar rune behind it.
The altar-to-colour mapping is a CHOICE with evidence: eight of the eleven share an exact
recolour destination with their rune item's own colours, and fire, chaos and law are the
nearest colour left. Nothing in the cache could settle those three.
